<thought>We have obtained the mass spectrum, which shows a molecular ion at m/z 194.0862 (likely [M+H]⁺). Subtracting a proton gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ~193.079 Da. The isotopic pattern (M+2 ≈ 33 % of the base peak) indicates the presence of a single chlorine atom. A plausible molecular formula that fits the exact mass and contains one Cl is C₁₀H₁₀ClN₂ (calculated monoisotopic mass = 193.053 Da, within typical instrument tolerance). To confirm the structure, the next inexpensive step is to acquire the ¹H NMR spectrum of the sample, which will reveal the number and type of hydrogen environments and help pinpoint the exact SMILES. 

Therefore, I will request the proton NMR spectrum.
